answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consider a juniper as the anchor of the cost. A summit stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a basalt hold...
